Information since February supports a “dovish hike” framing of the March 2017 FOMC move. The Committee raised the funds rate to 0.75–1.00% while emphasizing that policy remains accommodative, increases will be gradual, and decisions are data-dependent.

Beige Book insights reinforce this cautious stance:
- Activity: Modest-to-moderate growth across Districts; consumer spending generally steady but with softer auto sales in several areas.
- Labor/Wages: Labor markets tight, firms report hiring difficulties; wage growth modest to moderate rather than accelerating.
- Prices: Price pressures modest; inflation near, but not clearly above, 2%.
- Credit/CRE/Housing: Credit conditions mixed—signs of tighter standards and deteriorating performance in riskier consumer segments (notably autos) and some caution in CRE, while residential real estate is steadier with some easing in prime mortgage categories. Business loan demand mixed to slightly weaker at some institutions.

Taken together, the Beige Book points to steady growth with limited inflation pressure and emerging headwinds in certain credit pockets—consistent with a cautious, flexible approach rather than a hawkish pivot. Net tone: mildly positive but clearly restrained.
